Your glasses fog because the lenses are still cold from outside. When warm indoor air touches them, that thin layer of air cools below its dew point. The water vapour it was carrying condenses into tiny droplets on the glass.

The fog clears as the lenses warm to room temperature, which is why it lasts only a minute or two. Anti-fog coatings work by making the droplets spread into a flat, transparent film instead of scattering light.

None of this is specific to glasses. A cold drink "sweats" for the same reason, and so does a bathroom mirror after a hot shower.
